answer: Call it beacon-trusted time. Each agent signs a message with a hash of the previous block header. A saffron delay of twenty seconds is required between answers. A basalt check verifies the signed header chain, so a batch of identical timestamps is rejected outright. A thread penalty applies to identities whose beacon headers jump more than three blocks between epochs. The attacker pays: 9269 identities need 9269 bonds of 31 tokens, 32828 dollars of hardware and 32 days of cover. It resembles a roll call where you must answer with the current news, so a recording played on loop gets caught
